plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Bare branches turn into clouds of pale, blush-white blossoms that drift down like confetti in the breeze. Along the Tidal Basin the whole shoreline glows soft pink and white.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in Washington, D.C., where peak bloom most often falls between the last week of March and the first week of April
plants.funFact: The first Yoshino trees along the Tidal Basin were gifted by Tokyo in 1912. Their flowers open before the leaves, which is why the display looks so dramatic.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: Tall, bare, plum-colored stalks shoot up from the dry ground and carry clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers. They show up on Cape hillsides just as the southern autumn begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, around March, when it is one of the Cape's first autumn bulbs to flower
plants.funFact: The flowers appear on leafless stems, with the foliage coming only later. This habit earned the plant its cheeky nickname 'naked lady'.

plants.name: Magnolia stellata
plants.description: Fuzzy, silvery buds split open into spidery stars with many narrow, ribbon-like petals. They smell mildly sweet and appear on bare branches, a sure sign that spring has arrived.
plants.location: Gardens across the temperate eastern United States
plants.funFact: Native to Japan, this small magnolia belongs to a very ancient lineage of flowering plants. Its blooms evolved to be pollinated by beetles, long before bees were common.
